name: Checkpointing
summary: Undo Claude's file edits or roll the conversation back to an earlier prompt.
what: Claude Code records the state of the files it edits before each prompt you send. The rewind menu lists your prompts; pick one to restore the code, the conversation, or both to that point. The same menu can also shrink part of the conversation into a summary to free up context.

impact.title: Try things safely
impact.detail: Explore a different approach knowing you can return to where you started.

impact.title: Quick recovery
impact.detail: Revert edits that introduced a bug without leaving the session.

impact.title: More room in context
impact.detail: Summarize a long stretch of the conversation while keeping the rest intact.

howItWorks: Work as usual: every prompt that starts a turn creates a checkpoint automatically.
Run /rewind, or press Esc twice with an empty prompt, to open the rewind menu.
Select the prompt you want to go back to.
Choose what to restore: code and conversation, conversation only, or code only. Or choose one of the summarize options.
Keep using Git for anything permanent: changes made only by shell commands are not tracked, and checkpoints are for session-level recovery.

events.note: The /rewind command arrived, undoing code changes from a conversation.
